content:
Hi, I'm a master's student at ETH. I'm mechanizing Critch's Open-Source Game Theory in Lean 4 (bounded proof-search agents: "cooperate iff I can find a proof of at most k symbols that you cooperate with me", Löbian cooperation, bounded Löb, https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.07006). I have three questions about the provability side and this seems like the right place to ask.

The setting needs a bounded provability predicate □_k φ, "φ has an S-proof of length ≤ k", with bounded versions of the derivability conditions (something like □_a(φ→ψ) → □_b φ → □_{a+b+|ψ|} ψ) and Critch's parametric bounded Löb theorem. I did not arithmetize. Instead S is a budget-indexed inductive rule set where every rule carries an explicit transcript cost, and bounded Löb comes from an internal diagonal sentence. Soundness, bounded Löb and decidability of the relevant fragment are then proved rule by rule. My reasons: Critch himself only assumes an interface (bounded derivability conditions), not a specific theory. I don't know of any costed arithmetization in any prover; the closest thing I found is your RestrictedProvability. And the finite presentation keeps all the meta-theorems finite. The downside is that unprovability results silently assume the rule set is complete, and the cost of one rule (certifying that a k-bounded search failed, which is really a finite consistency statement) is calibrated against Pudlák's n^ε lower bound rather than derived from anything.

Questions:

  1. RestrictedProvability (∃ d < 2^e, Proof T d φ, plus the 2^e lower bound on proofs of the restricted Gödel sentence) is the closest formalized object to what I need. Have you thought about a bounded version of the ProvabilityAbstraction classes, i.e. HBL2/HBL3 with explicit cost shifts and a bounded löb_theorem? Is that something you'd consider in scope, or is restricted provability meant to stay a one-off for that lower bound?

  2. I'm considering an interface formalization: an abstract structure (budget-indexed □, monotonicity, soundness, costed HBL, bounded Löb), the game theory proved against it, my rule set as one instance, and an arithmetized instance in the style of RestrictedProvable left as an explicit obligation for later. Would you build that as a budget-indexed variant of ProvabilityAbstraction.Provability, or differently?

  3. From a proof theory point of view, is a rule set with costs a legitimate object for these theorems, or does it look like a fudge? I'd rather hear it now than at my defense.

Happy to share more (code, the per-rule cost justifications) with anyone who's interested.
